newsitem.title: USA: Pier 1 sees sales growth, backs estimates.
newsitem.headline: Pier 1 sees sales growth, backs estimates.

text.p: Pier 1 Imports Inc, which operates more than 700 stores selling decorative home furnishings, expects sales this year of more than $1 billion and has targeted sales growth of 12 to 15 percent over the next five years.

"Certainly sales this year will exceed $1 billion," said Clark Johnson, chairman of the Fort Worth, Texas, specialty retailer. For its fiscal year ended March 31, 1997, Pier One generated sales of $947.1 million.

"Our strategy is to continue to develop programs that grow our same-store sales six to seven percent a year, net square footage six to eight percent a year, both domestically and internationally," he said.
Those goals are expected to be accomplished through internal growth and not through acquisition. "We still see opportunity for internal growth," he said.
Pier 1 has 670 stores in the United States and Canada and has identified about 400 sites for store openings in those countries. "So we have plenty of opportunity for growth," he said.
Pier 1 will open 55 stores this year and at least 65 a year over the next three years starting next year, he said.
"We feel through a combination of internal growth domestically and opening new markets around the world that there is plenty of opportunity for Pier 1 to grow," Johnson said.
In addition to Canada, the retailer operates nine stores in Mexico, five units in Japan and 15 units in Britain. It also has four stores in Puerto Rico.
Johnson said the British stores would "be solidly profitable this year," compared with a loss of $900,000 last year.

Pier 1 has benefited from a shift to spending on home furnishings and away from apparel. "Clearly, we are in the right segment of the retail business," he said, citing record home sales and favorable mortgage rates.

About 33 percent of Pier 1's business is generated from furniture sales, including wicker, wood and glass; about 29 percent from decorative accessories including pillows; 15 percent from housewares, dishes, wine glasses; about 13 percent from bed and bath items; and about 10 percent from seasonal items for Christmas and Easter.
